insight: There's been no rain at all lately, so stormwater runoff isn't a factor right now. The model's main signals right now: hours since high tide is lowering risk — the timing relative to high tide affects how concentrated bacteria are at the shoreline; high tide level is lowering risk — a high tide can mobilize bacteria held in wet sand and push the waterline toward outfalls; and daytime high temperature is lowering risk — warmer conditions can help bacteria survive longer (and track the season). The most recent sample, 5 days ago, was excellent at 10 MPN/100mL. It's a naturally clean, well-flushed open-coast beach (unsafe only ~3% of the time), so outside of storms it's reliably safe.
